intent: I kept the wheel track at 0.18 to maintain the improved lateral stability that reduces off-track failures. The rear sensors remain at y = -0.035 to provide early line detection on sharp turns, as this positioning has shown promise. I kept sensor size at 0.016 for noise robustness. Given the integrator feedback that the controller needs stronger gains and sensor weights to exploit this geometry, I focus this iteration on geometry stability and early detection, expecting the controller to leverage these for better progress and fewer line loss events.
rationale: The last race data and integrator feedback show that increasing wheel track to 0.18 and moving rear sensors back to y = -0.035 improved early line detection and lateral stability but the controller still struggles with early off-track failures and line loss events. The geometry changes have provided a stable and early sensing platform, but the controller needs to be more aggressive and responsive to exploit this. Therefore, I keep the geometry unchanged this iteration to allow the controller to adapt fully to these stable and early sensing conditions. I expect this to improve completion and progress metrics by reducing line loss and off-track events. I request measurements of completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, and line_loss_events to verify these effects.
